correctness.rationale: For d≥2 and u∈C⁵, Taylor expansion of Hε fε Hε⁻¹ with Hε=id+εu and v=du−u∘T_d cancels the O(ε) term and produces Gε=T_d+ε²u′(d·)v+O_C²(ε³). Consequently (log Gε′−log d)/ε²→φ=w′/d in C¹. The log derivative changes under conjugacy by a bounded coboundary, so Green–Kubo variance is invariant. Bernoulli coding with uniform inverse-branch contraction bounds correlations by Cλ^(−n/2), proving continuity and σ²(ε)/ε⁴→V_Td(φ). For u=−sin(2πx)/(2π), φ has modes −1/2 cos2πx, 3/2 cos6πx, −cos8πx: exact independent Fourier arithmetic gives covariances 7/4,0,1/4,0 thereafter, yielding 9/4. Uniform expansion holds |ε|<1/4 for this example; the general result is sufficiently small |ε|.
residual_risks: No assertion that the coefficient is positive for arbitrary u; finite sampled ε from packaged script is not the universal argument.
